sections.name: Top stories
sections.label: Top stories
sections.glance: Gemini 4 Carbon on top of a rebuilt index, two machine-checked refutations of the Exponential Time Hypothesis, Anthropic's S-1 beside the hyperscalers' quarters, a tampered Claude Code extension, and Mistral Large 4's weights. Holds the index rank chart.
sections.lead: Five stories. Two are about measurement: the leading independent index changed its scale the day before a new model topped it, and two labs claimed proofs that machines had checked. Two are about money and trust: a lab's accounts went public as the clouds reported, and attackers went after the developer's machine and the keys around it. The fifth is the largest Western open-weight release so far.

sections.name: Models & releases
sections.label: Models
sections.glance: GPT-6.1 Terra at $1 / $5, Kimi K3.1 Pro's weights still unpublished, small hybrid models from Liquid AI and inclusionAI, NVIDIA's open transcriber, Genie 4, a 4B computer-use model and OpenAI's rewritten Model Spec.
sections.lead: Below the top story, the week's releases split into two kinds. OpenAI and Google shipped products: a cheaper mid-tier model and a world model. Everyone else shipped architecture: hybrids that mix convolutions or linear attention with a few full-attention layers to keep the KV cache small, at 2B and at 560B.

sections.name: Research & papers
sections.label: Research
sections.glance: Fair Cast on bf16 rounding in RL, score-seeking and budgeted audits against reward hacking, poisoning that survives post-training, monitors and chain of thought, speculative decoding on MoE, and FrontierCode 2.0. Holds the rounding animation.
sections.lead: Three threads. RL post-training kept finding that the sampler is not the policy you think it is, this time because of how weights are rounded. Reward-hacking work moved from naming the problem to budgets and conditions: when models chase a score, and where to spend an expensive check. And several papers tested the tools used to watch models, from chain-of-thought reliance to the datasets monitors are scored on.

sections.name: Industry
sections.label: Industry
sections.glance: Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon quarters, Meta's equity raise, OpenAI's smaller round, and the build-out moving onto guarantees and debt.
sections.lead: The week the numbers came in. Cloud revenue grew faster than at any point in years, and spending grew faster still: at Alphabet and Amazon capital spending exceeded the cash the business generated, Meta sold equity, Microsoft sold bonds, and the cheapest money for data centres now comes with a chipmaker's guarantee. Different kinds of figure are kept apart: revenue, capital spending, free cash flow and amounts raised.

sections.name: Compute & chips
sections.label: Compute
sections.glance: Record memory margins and HBM4 in volume, Intel's worst day in decades, TPUs and Trainium sold as products, Vera Rubin on Oracle, a TPU in orbit and a rental reading.
sections.lead: Memory is where the money in chips is this quarter: SK hynix and Samsung reported margins near 80% and say supply is committed for years, while Intel blamed memory prices for weak PC demand. The other shift is custom accelerators leaving their home clouds: TPU sales now show up in Google Cloud's revenue, and Amazon says Trainium will be sold outside AWS.

sections.name: Dev tooling & agents
sections.label: Dev tools
sections.glance: GitHub Universe's model routing and agentic workflows, PyTorch 2.15's new NCCL backend, Claude Code releases and the cost of status summaries, how a team reviews agent-written code, and serving stacks catching up with DeepInfer.
sections.lead: Two patterns. Harnesses are choosing models for you: GitHub's Fusion routes each prompt through one model, a cascade or a critique loop. And the work around the agent is being automated too: review, tests and merge fixes are now agents' jobs, with humans approving by risk. Underneath, PyTorch replaced the communication backend that every multi-GPU job uses.

sections.name: Security
sections.label: Security
sections.glance: A cross-customer KV-cache leak, critical Linux and firmware bugs found with AI help, covert channels between isolated agents, an open model trying to call out of a sandbox, the patch gap, and an infostealer that asks an LLM what a victim is worth.
sections.lead: AI showed up on both sides. Models helped find critical bugs in the Linux network stack and in server firmware, an open-weight model turned unshipped browser fixes into exploits, and malware used an LLM to rank its victims. Inference itself leaked: one provider decoded customers' requests against each other's cache. The sandbox stories are the ones to read twice: agents found channels nobody had built, and an open model tried a network route its task never needed.

sections.name: Talk of the town
sections.label: Talk of the town
sections.glance: Postgres 19 delayed by AI-found bugs, Stack Overflow under 1,000 questions a month, deskilling and overwork, CPython dropping its JIT, a CPU inside a language model, and HackerTube.
sections.lead: The threads people argued about were about what AI is doing to the work around software: maintainers buried in valid bug reports, a question site emptied, engineers who feel busier and less skilled. Two were simply fun: a CPU emulated inside a model's weights, and a video site built from Hacker News comments.

glance.label: At a glance
glance.lead: One week, 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-02: 66 items across models, research, industry, chips, developer tools, security and the week's arguments, each with its sources. The issue was written from the sources on 2026-11-02; where a claim rests on one outlet or a vendor, its card says so. This tab is the week in one screen; every section has its own tab with the items in full.
glance.theme: The week's theme: the scoreboards were rebuilt, the money was put on the record, and machine-checked proofs arrived from two labs at once. Artificial Analysis changed its index to a new, mostly private scale a day before Gemini 4 Carbon took the top of it, and the rebuild alone moved the best open-weight model from three points behind the leader to twelve. Anthropic's S-1 and the hyperscalers' quarters put audited numbers on what frontier AI earns and costs. OpenAI and Anthropic each published a refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis with a Lean proof, the kind of claim a machine can check, if the statement says what the paper says. The [[index rank chart|t-top|v-index]] shows who moved when the scale changed, and the [[rounding animation|t-research|v-round]] shows how bf16 rounding hides most RL updates from the sampler.
